scope: Disk same-key stress accounting and bounded retry policy; no engine implementation change

references.application: Retain the engine TxnConflict contract and its locked commit validation. A failed optimistic commit must be retried with a fresh transaction. Proposed queue/precheck changes are excluded from this PR because they did not resolve the measured tail condition.
references.intentional_difference: Alopex retains its global commit serialization; RocksDB parallel validation uses ordered lock buckets. No claim of identical concurrency protocol.
references.license: GPL-2.0 or Apache-2.0; consulted design, no code copied.
references.test_classification: existing handwritten regression; no new reference fixture copied

references.application: Retry fresh transactions within the existing shared 60-second scenario budget. Preserve the existing five-second lack-of-progress watchdog. Require 2000 successes, 2000 logical latency samples and zero exhausted writes; record all conflicts and all retry waiting in latency.
references.intentional_difference: SQLite waits on locks up to a busy timeout; Alopex must create a fresh transaction after TxnConflict. Delay policy is a workload policy, not an engine-level guarantee.
references.license: Public domain; inspected, no test code copied.

references.application: Full Jitter over a 16ms maximum interval (the same cap as the prior 20-retry candidate) with a deterministic mixer. Stop retries at the shared scenario deadline; preserve the core fsync/TxnConflict behavior.
references.intentional_difference: The SDK code uses crypto randomness and returns a fixed maximum above its attempt cap. This reproducible stress workload uses a deterministic mixer, a positive microsecond floor, and retains jitter at the cap as in the Full Jitter design; the shared 60-second scenario deadline is separate. This is not a production SDK port.
references.license: Apache-2.0; consulted implementation and tests, no source copied.

benchmark.design: 36 independent processes: 4 execution-model labels x 3 policy arms x 3 alternating trials. Same original-engine binary in all arms; 100 workers x 20 writes. Different completed-work counts are not evidence of a throughput speedup.
benchmark.engine_base: 02d30d1e20fb914149245f3e23018d6e56f009fa; its commit_write_set implementation matches the focused PR parent f8739720. Exact PR checkout was separately exercised by the eight-case repository stress test.
benchmark.hardware: Apple M5 Pro, 18 logical CPUs, 48 GiB RAM, macOS 27.0.1 arm64; Rust release opt-level=3, LTO, one codegen unit.
benchmark.limitations: Both Sync labels use 100 OS threads. AsyncSingle runs synchronous commits on one runtime thread. These results establish completion/accounting for this fixture, not a five-second tail-latency guarantee or production-engine speedup.

rejected_experiments: FIFO snapshot writer tickets increased deadline failures and were removed.
Checked and cancellation-aware writer queues did not eliminate five-second tails and were removed. No engine queue or early-precheck change is included.
Equal/Full Jitter trials with a 128ms cap and a five-second logical-operation deadline retained failures. Those raw results remain failed diagnostics.
contract_correction: The pre-existing operation_timeout=5s in common/watchdog.rs evaluates time since global progress; it is not a per-logical-write latency guarantee. An agent-added five-second logical deadline was therefore an additional diagnostic, not the existing acceptance contract. Preserve its failures and report observed tails rather than claiming they were fixed.
